topic: Context rot: 4 ways agents keep context small on long tasks (Anthropic engineering)
text:
Your agent doesn't forget because the context window is full. It gets worse as it fills.

Anthropic's engineering team calls this context rot: recall accuracy declines as tokens pile up, across all models. Their advice is to treat context as a finite resource with diminishing returns.

Four techniques they describe for long tasks:

1. Compaction: summarize a nearly full window, then start fresh with the summary
2. Note-taking: write a NOTES.md or to-do list outside the window, read it back later
3. Sub-agents: focused work in a clean window, returning only a short summary
4. Just-in-time retrieval: keep file paths and queries, load data only when needed

My rule of thumb: clear old tool results first, it's the cheapest win. Add the fancier techniques only when a real failure shows up.

Which of these would you try first on a long-running agent, and why?
